title: China Marks National Day with Flag Ceremonies and Mao Tributes
text:
China celebrates National Day with flag-raising events, Mao Zedong honors, and a Beijing banquet, as Xi Jinping vows rejuvenation amid global tensions.
On Thursday, the Chinese Communist Party marked the 1949 establishment of the People's Republic of China with nationwide flag-raising ceremonies, government-backed activities honoring Mao Zedong, and a grand banquet for communist elites in Beijing. The main event drew over 100,000 people to Tiananmen Square for the dawn flag-raising at 6:00 a.m. Similar ceremonies were held in Tibet, East Turkistan, and the disputed South China Sea. President Xi Jinping addressed the elite banquet on Wednesday night.
Historical Context of National Day
China's National Day commemorates the formal founding of the People's Republic of China in 1949. This year, the government encouraged citizens to celebrate Mao Zedong's achievements over the following week. Mao's legacy includes the Long March, where about 100,000 people walked over 6,000 miles to escape Kuomintang forces, with only roughly 4,000 survivors, including Mao.
After becoming the nation's dictator, Mao implemented deadly programs such as the Great Leap Forward, which is estimated to have killed 45 million people. He also architected the one-child policy, forcing mothers to kill any children after their first for decades. State media claims the policy prevented millions of births, but critics highlight its brutal enforcement.
Xi Jinping's Vision for Rejuvenation
Xi Jinping, fresh from a visit to Washington last week, delivered a speech at the banquet on Wednesday night. He stressed the inevitability of great national rejuvenation under the Party's leadership. Xi said that with confidence and steady progress, success will belong to the great CPC, the Chinese people, and the People's Republic of China.
He expressed pride in New China's achievements and confidence in Chinese modernization. Xi asked the people to trust the Politburo's plan for rejuvenation without detailing public policy. The term national rejuvenation often implies making China the world's dominant hegemon and diminishing America's superpower status.
Xi also promised to promote a community with a shared future for humanity, contributing certainty and positive energy to a turbulent world. State media noted he only briefly mentioned Taiwan, a sovereign state that China claims as a renegade province, and the ongoing capture of Hong Kong and Macau.
Ceremonies and Celebrations Across Regions
Wednesday was also Martyrs' Day, honoring millions who died in Mao's quest for totalitarian communism. Xi attended a wreath-laying ceremony. In Tiananmen Square, an 18-meter-high flower basket with the words Blessings to the Motherland stood at the center, as visitors gathered the night before.
State media reported quieter celebrations in East Turkistan, where the Communist Party has engaged in genocide against Uyghur, Kazakh, and Kyrgyz people for about a decade. Police from the Kalabulake border station patrolled the Gobi and mountain passes, cleaning boundary markers and repainting inscriptions red before offering National Day wishes.
The Communist Party also raised its flag over the Scarborough Shoal, a Philippine territory, on Thursday. An astronaut said that across deserts, mountains, and islands, generations have spent 70 years striving to create the glory of China's space program.
